newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan not considering easing ban on Taiwan pork.
newsitem.headline: Japan not considering easing ban on Taiwan pork.

text.p: Japan's Agriculture Ministry said on Wednesday that it is not considering a partial easing of its import ban on Taiwanese pork, which was imposed on March 21 after an outbreak of foot and mouth disease among Taiwan's hog population.
Earlier on Wednesday, Taiwan's Economic Minister Wang Chih-kang said that, after negotiations, Japan was considering easing a ban on imports of Taiwan pork.

But Katsuaki Sugiura, deputy director of the Japanese Agriculture Ministry's animal health division, told Reuters: "Our import ban on Taiwan pork is still effective. We don't know why he made such a statement in Taiwan."
Wang's comment was later modified by Taiwan's economic ministry to mean that Japan had agreed to allow entry of 13,000 tonnes of frozen pork already in Japanese ports, not to partially ease the ban.
But Sugiura said this was also not the case.
"Our decision was to stop all Taiwanese pork imports, even if it is waiting in Japan's customs. That decision is unchanged at the moment," he said.
Japan imported 653,176 tonnes of pork in 1996, Finance Ministry data showed. Of that, 266,225 tonnes or 40.7 percent came from Taiwan, its largest supplier.
